verdictBasis: The four scoped findings are fixed on the paths they named: QE-R7B-R2-01, -R2-02 (the factual re-plan), -R2-03 and the QE-R7B-01 residual all resolve with plan-level evidence that fails on FREEZE-2 and passes on these bytes, and the QE-R7B-R2-05 classification as the R18 path holds. But one new MAJOR finding sits on the block-choice paths this gate must check in full: QE-R7B1-01, a block-choice question pre-empts the handler's clinical screen. A review that reports pain with an exercise (reason-based substitution) or an illness interruption gets the non-clinical question 'Block choices are made in the weekly review…' instead of CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED; the reference state records ASK, so the clinical pending is lost. Since R7-B.1's QE-R7B-R2-02 correction, with a correction in the same review, that question also carries a prescription proposal (the factual re-plan of the sessions ahead), where the same review without the choice routes to a human and proposes nothing. This contradicts the SSCTR record B0-C06 condition 8 ('passes the clinical screen first'), SSCTR D08 and the R7-A rule that a clinical route proposes nothing. Two pre-existing MINOR findings and one observation are recorded beside it. They do not block on their own.

blockers.evidence: Recheck probes (copies): n7 N7a, N7b, N7c and n8 N7d FAIL on FREEZE-2 -> PASS. j2-novice-persistence: 15 decision timelines on strength-NONE athletes (SKILL_MISMATCH and preference substitutions; schedule changes 2->4, 2->3, 4->2 and 2->4 from a later week; equipment kettlebell-only, bodyweight-only, added, a one-week window; goal changes; three sequences) followed by up to five weekly reviews. J2a: the stored capped templates follow the context, with no set-aside exercise and no missing equipment. J2b: capped exactly when the state is. J2c: the next review reproduces the decision's selection. J2d: released -> corrected re-caps from the stored context and keeps earlier decisions. J2e: an earlier segment keeps its context. All 0 failures. On FREEZE-2, J2a-J2d fail. j2f: a held release (boundary week not earned) plans capped weeks from the stored templates; PASS (FAIL on FREEZE-2). j2g: a change reaching an earlier context segment and the later context stays consistent; PASS (FAIL on FREEZE-2). Planned, released, executed, corrected and current program authority stay distinct: the cap stays in the state (densityCappedAt) and the templates follow the context.

n-delta N1, N1b and n8 N1 FAIL on FREEZE-2 -> PASS. j1-block-choice-paths: 132 cases (17 review kinds x 3 choices x correction or none on a strength novice; 5 kinds x 3 choices x 2 on a graduated runner). n-delta N3 FAIL on FREEZE-2 -> PASS. j3-skill-mismatch-fallback J3a: SKILL_MISMATCH of every exercise in use in a grid of up to 64 programs (362 substitutions; 58 whose substitute needs extra equipment), then a permanent loss and a one-week window of that equipment (116 cases) and the next weekly reviews to week 8. 0 slots of the replaced exercise take it back, a rung above it, or a configuration above the substitute's skill. QE-R7B-R2-05.evidence: j6-r205-classification: two-day novice moved to four days in week 1, then a decision on day 0 of week 2. Week 2 is capped in all four contract paths: week 1 reviewed with nothing reported, with part reported, with all reported, and the change made after the week-1 review. It is also capped when week 1 is complete but unreviewed. Week 2 is uncapped only when week 1 gets no gating weekly review: skipped, a mid-week review only, or partly reported and unreviewed. That is R18 ('every elapsed week receives its gating weekly review'). FREEZE-2 gives the same classification.

newFindings.origin: PRE-EXISTING, AGGRAVATED BY R7-B.1. The clinical bypass was introduced at FREEZE-2 by the R7-B fix cycle (QE-R7B-08's early block-choice question); FREEZE-1 routes all 16 cases to a human (j1b on a git archive of 4995d58). R7-B.1's QE-R7B-R2-02 correction kept that precedence (choiceAsk is decided before the handler) and routed the question through withFactualReplan. With a correction in the same review, it now returns a prescription proposal on a review that reports pain or illness: 4 of the 12 bypassed cases, 0 on FREEZE-2.
newFindings.area: block-choice paths x clinical screen; catalog/runtime binding (B0-C06 condition 8); R7-A clinical rule in withFactualReplan
newFindings.summary: src/r6-adaptation.mjs:363-364 decides the block-choice question (any review kind other than a complete weekly review, or mid-week) before the handler runs, and :329 rejects an unrecognised choice before it. So the handler-level clinical screens never run: exerciseSubstitution (:537: pain, injury or a clinical text -> CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED) and returnAfterPause (:1212: a clinical interruption reason). The review answers a non-clinical question. Its reference state records pending ASK, not CLINICAL, so the clinical stickiness later reviews would carry is lost. With a correction and a recognised choice, the ASK carries the factual re-plan of the sessions ahead, including the exercise reported painful. The second block-choice path already yields to the clinical route (:365, decision0.status !== 'CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED'); the first does not. R7-B.1's closure record states 'The clinical screen and the questions are unchanged and come first'. That holds without a choice, not with one. The conformance entry SSCTR:B0-C06#c8 (IMPLEMENTED) is contradicted on this path; the conformance check is structural and does not see it.
newFindings.authority: SSCTR record B0-C06 condition 8: 'Reason-based substitution keeps precedence over cadence but passes the clinical screen first: pain, injury, illness or a functional limitation routes CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED for the dependent scope'. SSCTR D08: illness never gets a nonclinical recipe. R7-A withFactualReplan (src/r6-adaptation.mjs:1071, :1073-1074): 'A clinical route proposes nothing (no dependent prescription)'.

newFindings.area: QE-R7B-05 class through a state transition (return); HistoricalState vs PlanningProjection
newFindings.summary: The return reads stateAtBreak -> evidenceState in the HISTORY reading (src/r6-adaptation.mjs:1154). That reading judges each week under its own context (:952, skn = skj) and never starts a cap that a schedule change from two to more days started (src/r6-program.mjs:838 under the two-day context; strengthAtBreak never starts it). The return's entry therefore has no density, densityCappedAt (r6-program.mjs:100) is false, and the sessions still ahead in the re-entry week are planned on the uncapped split. The cap returns at the next week transition. An intake-capped athlete keeps the cap through the same return: HISTORY has the intake density. All elapsed weeks are reviewed here, so this is not the R18 path.

Event-week guard (QE-R7B-OBS-04) as a state transition, j5. It reads the evidence of the decision's own week. A missed substitute stays out of the event weeks. A correction that retracts its execution removes it from the sessions ahead (REPLAN_FROM_EVIDENCE). HistoricalState never reads the projection (lastPerformedAt null unless executed). j8: the same through a return reported in the taper. FREEZE-2 fails both.

projectedOnly semantics: the decision's own projection may show the substitute in later event weeks (j5 'projectedInEventWeeksByTheDecision'). The weekly review of the week before re-plans from evidence; the case that keeps it unreviewed is R18.
